resolutions.researcher_notes: Hydrocarbons Technology (GlobalData), project profile: 'Construction on the project began in the first quarter of 2016 and was completed in early 2017. The pipeline came on line in March 2017.' Natural Gas Intelligence (Mar 22, 2017, cited from its seed URL, which now redirects to an unrelated current article on the live site -- confirmed via Wayback capture 2019-08-17, which passes on the full body text): 'The Trans-Pecos system is slated to come online March 31, according to a company spokeswoman.' Two distinct publishers agree the pipeline entered service in 2017 and neither source, nor any other source checked (Business Wire in-service announcement, DeSmog Blog Jan 2017, both discussed below), indicates it has since gone offline -- supports Status=operating. Live naturalgasintel.com URL 200s but silently redirects to a different, unrelated current article (the 2017 article ID no longer resolves on the live site, confirmed by curl -- a soft-redirect, not a 404), so the Wayback snapshot is proposed in its place per the blocked/moved-origin rule.

Railroad Commission of Texas Form T-4/T-4A permit application (Apr 6, 2015, Permit No. 09352; hosted on DocumentCloud, contributed by Marfa Public Radio reporter Travis Bubenik -- this IS the government document, not a navigation surface): the fluid-transported checkbox lists 'Specify Natural Gas' for the pipeline. Note the DocumentCloud VIEWER page (the seed URL) is a client-rendered shell with no server-side text -- verified its raw OCR text via the underlying asset endpoint (`assets.documentcloud.org/documents/2062745/trans-pecos-pipeline-t4-permit.txt`, same document, direct text) and propose that URL instead since it is the one that actually carries the checkable content; both resolve to the same filed document. Natural Gas Intelligence (Wayback, see Status unit) independently describes it throughout as a 'natural gas pipeline' carrying gas from the Waha Hub. Two independent origins (a Texas state regulatory filing and a trade-press article) agree.

Same RRC T-4/T-4A permit (see Fuel unit for the URL note): the permit's own cover certification reads 'INITIAL PERMIT FOR APPROXIMATELY 143 MILES OF PROPOSED 42" TO TRANSMISSION LINE', and question 3 of the application form ('Check detailed purpose(s) for which described pipeline will be used') is answered Transmission. Single explicit source for the literal word 'transmission' -- Natural Gas Intelligence and Hydrocarbons Technology both describe the pipeline as a long-haul interstate/intrastate gas line consistent with transmission service but neither uses the word itself, so kept at medium/independent=false rather than overclaiming.

CONCERN: the sources found put construction starting earlier than the sheet's September 2016. Hydrocarbons Technology's project profile states plainly: 'Construction Started Q1 2016' and 'Construction on the project began in the first quarter of 2016.' The Dallas Morning News (Jun 10, 2016), in a piece about celebrity opposition, is headlined/subtitled 'As construction starts, they're asking Dallas energy mogul Kelcy Warren to change his company's plans' -- consistent with construction already underway by June 2016, i.e. before Q3. Neither source names September 2016 specifically, and I found no source that does. Not proposing either as a ref for ConstructionYear/Month=2016-09 since both actually point to an earlier date; flagging for Update to check whether the sheet's September falls in a different phase (e.g. a specific segment or the Mexico-side/Presidio Crossing facilities, versus the main Texas intrastate line) or is a data error. Other seed citations from 2015 (Truthout May 2015, OGJ Nov 2015, Texas Monthly Sept 2015, Fronteras Apr 2015, the RRC T-4 permit itself Apr 2015) all predate any construction phase and describe permitting/eminent-domain fights, not a construction start date, so none of them bear on this unit either way.

Same two sources as Status: Hydrocarbons Technology ('completed in early 2017. The pipeline came on line in March 2017'), Natural Gas Intelligence (Mar 22, 2017 article: 'slated to come online March 31'). Grupo Carso's own 2016 Annual Report (see SegmentCost unit) independently corroborates the year with 'Start of operations: February 2017' for the Waha-Presidio project -- a third, primary owner-side source, all agreeing on 2017 (specific month varies Feb/Mar across sources -- plausibly commissioning vs. formal commercial in-service dates -- but the sheet only asserts StartYear1=2017 with no month, so this is not a conflict). Tier high/independent true off the two trade-press sources alone; Carso's report adds a third agreeing origin.

Natural Gas Intelligence: 'Trans-Pecos will have capacity to transport 1.4 Bcf/d.' Hydrocarbons Technology: 'transports approximately 1.4 billion cubic feet (bcf) of natural gas a day.' 1.4 Bcf/d = 1,400 MMcf/d, an exact match to the sheet's Capacity=1400.00 MMcf/d. Two distinct publishers agree exactly.

Hydrocarbons Technology: 'The Trans-Pecos pipeline is 148mi (238km) long.' Natural Gas Intelligence: 'the 148-mile, 42-inch diameter pipeline.' Grupo Carso's 2016 Annual Report (co-owner's own report, listing its Waha-Presidio project): 'Length of 238 kilometers and diameter of 42 inches' -- 238 km converts to 147.9 mi, matching 148 mi almost exactly. Three distinct, independent origins (trade press x2, owner-company primary report) all agree. Note: the RRC's Apr-2015 T-4 permit application (see Fuel unit) states 'Approximately 143 miles' -- this is the pre-construction proposal filed at the initial-permit stage, ~5 miles short of the three sources' 148/238km as-built figure; read as initial engineering estimate vs. final built length, not a conflict, and not proposed as a ref for this reason.

Hydrocarbons Technology: '42in in diameter.' Natural Gas Intelligence: '42-inch diameter pipeline.' RRC T-4 permit: 'PROPOSED 42" ... TRANSMISSION LINE' and the system-information worksheet lists '42" O.D.' Three independent origins (two trade press, one state regulatory filing) all agree exactly on 42 inches.

Natural Gas Intelligence: 'originates at the Waha Hub outside Fort Stockton, TX, in northern Pecos County ... terminates at the U.S.-Mexico boundary near Presidio, TX.' Hydrocarbons Technology: 'It originates in the Waha hub outside Fort Stockton in northern Pecos County ... to the US-Mexico boundary near Presidio, Texas.' RRC T-4 permit: lists the pipeline's counties as Brewster, Pecos, Presidio, TX, and a January 2015 cover letter names the specific route: 'Pipeline Name: Waha to Presido [sic], Size 42", Length 755,040 ft / 143 miles, County Pecos, Presidio, Brewster.' Three independent origins (two trade press, one state regulatory filing) agree the route runs from Fort Stockton/Waha Hub, Pecos County, TX to Presidio, TX at the Texas-Mexico border, matching StartLocation=Fort Stockton / EndLocation=Presidio exactly.

Hydrocarbons Technology: 'The $767m pipeline transports clean-burning natural gas from Pecos, Brewster and Presidio counties.' Grupo Carso's own 2016 Annual Report, in its Waha-Presidio project listing: 'Net Present Value of USD $767 million offered.' Two independent origins -- one trade press, one a co-owner's own primary financial disclosure -- agree exactly on $767 million, matching the sheet's SegmentCost=767,000,000 USD precisely.

CONCERN: no source located anywhere names the operating entity 'Texas Pecos Pipeline LLC.' Every primary and secondary source found -- the RRC T-4/T-4A permit ('Does the above named operator conduct or control the economic Operations on the pipeline? ... Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC'), MasTec's own SEC 10-K Exhibit 21 subsidiaries list ('Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC (33% owned by MasTec TPP, LLC) (16% owned by Energy Transfer Mexicana, LLC) (51% owned by Carso Energy Corp.)'), and Hydrocarbons Technology ('operated by the ETP Consortium') -- names the entity 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC', never 'Texas Pecos Pipeline LLC'. Also checked SEC EDGAR full-text search for the exact phrase 'Texas Pecos Pipeline' / 'Texas-Pecos Pipeline': the hits that came back (Kinder Morgan 10-Ks) are unrelated -- fetched the 2016 10-K itself and confirmed its only 'Pecos' references are to the wholly separate Kinder Morgan CO2/EOR 'Pecos pipeline' (McCamey, TX to Iraan, TX) and 'Pecos Carbon Dioxide Pipeline', not this project at all. This reads as a data-entry variant/transposition of 'Trans-Pecos' -> 'Texas Pecos' rather than a distinct real entity. Not proposing a ref since every candidate source's exact wording would not literally match the cell's current text (risk of an orphan/mismatched ref); flagging for Update to consider correcting Operator to 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC', which is fully documented above.

MasTec, Inc.'s SEC 10-K Exhibit 21 (Affiliated Entities, filed for FY2015): lists 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC (33% owned by MasTec TPP, LLC) (16% owned by Energy Transfer Mexicana, LLC) (51% owned by Carso Energy Corp.)' -- an exact match to the sheet's three-way split (Owner1 16% / Owner2 Carso Energy 51% / Owner3 MasTec 33%). Grupo Carso's 2016 Annual Report independently corroborates the 51% figure ('Carso Energy stake: 51.0%'). Two independent primary/legal-filing origins (a public company's SEC exhibit, a public company's own annual report) agree on the percentage split. Note for Update's awareness (not raised as a full CONCERN since the substance -- three owners, exact percentages -- is corroborated): the sheet's Owner1 is labeled 'ETP Legacy' at 16%, while the SEC filing names that same 16% stakeholder 'Energy Transfer Mexicana, LLC' -- likely a naming/labeling variant for the Energy Transfer-affiliated 16% owner rather than a substantive discrepancy, since Owner2/Owner3 names and all three percentages match exactly.
